# Battle of Nikitovka

Battle of Nikitovka was fought between the Italian forces under the command of Giovanni Messe and Soviet Union during the Eastern Front of World War II.The 80th Regiment "Roma" successfully defeated a surprise attack of the Russians and occupied Nikitovka. However they found themselves completely blocked by the Russians at Nikitovka, several attempts were made by the other Italian deployment but they failed. On 13 November another battle was fought as a final attempt for a breakout which was successful and the Russians retreated. Nikitovka remained under Axis specially Italian occupation untill it was recaptured by the Soviets on August 1943 in the Donbas strategic offensive.
Background
The C.S.I.R was ordered to invade and capture the strategic areas of Gorlovka and Nikitovka. However these battles would caused many casualties for the italian units, having no choice left Giovanni Messe futher encouraged his men and started marching towards Gorlovka and Nikitovka. On night of 22nd October the Italian amry moved towards Kryvyi Rih and capturing the area after facing some resistance from the Russians. Then the army charged at Skotovoye and after a brief engagement forced the enemies to retreat. After passing through Grishino on 23 October, the Italian forces captured Scelesnoje after defeating the superior Russian forces.
On 1 November the Russians for an unknown reason retreated towards Gorlovka and Rikovo, the 3rd Bersaglieri Regiment immediately advanced upon the retreating Russians, the Italians soon defeated the Russians and captured the locality. The 70th and 80th Regiment encounter resistance by the enemies and the rebels at Gorlovka. The fighting had to be distributed over the entire street layout with some fighting being done house by house, in sub-zero temperatures, constantly under the threat of snipers that required the fighters to be separated into smaller groups in order to reduce the chance of being an easy target. The Italians successfully captured Gorlovka at dawn on 2 November and the Russians retreated towards Novohryhorivka.
Battle
On 2nd November the 80th Regiment of the Axis forces after their victory at Gorlovka, advanced into Trudovaya but found themselves attacked by the Russians in the vicinity of Nikitovka. Since there was a gap of nearly 40 km between the Italian Royal Army and 17th Panzer Division the Russians tried to take advantage of this situation. The 80th Regiment reacted immediately by launching a counteroffensive and forcing the Russians to retreat. Then the Italians occupied Nikitovka on 6th November 1941. However the 80th Regiment "Roma" had advanced too far away from other Italian deployment and found themselves completely stuck and blocked by the Russians in Nikitovka.
Several attempts to unblock the 80th Regiment "Roma" were made, the first attempt was made on 10 November by 79th Infantry Regiment but they were defeated and forced to retreat on the same day another attempt  was made by the 3rd Bersaglieri Regiment but that too ended in a failure. The situation was desperate as they had run out of food, water and ammunition and the temperature was low, freezing their guns and men. During the battle an episode of a Russian woman named Juliana Andr occurred, who despite the disapproval of Colonel Chiaramonti headed towards the well in the open battlefield to fetch water. She trusted her womanhood even though she felt tormented by the men who were supposed to be her enemies but she had watched them suffer for too long but on the way she was struck by a sudden burst of gunfire of the Soviets. The 80th Regiment "Roma" buried her alongside the soldiers of the Regiment with all honours they were given.
By 11 November the situation became desperate, the recovery of wounded and resupplies were impossible. On 12 November the 3rd Bersaglieri Regiment under the command of Aminto Caretto were able to penetrate inside Nikitovka but they were mate by heavy barrage by the Russians were subjected and forced to retreat. At Afternoon when Colonel Chiaramonti was informed about the defeat and retreat of Aminto Caretto he planned at attack in the dark, the Italians were successful in this attempt. An Italian officer named Rosario Randazzo even after lossing his arm kept firing the machine gun through his mouth, he was honoured with a Golden Medal later on. A sudden, violent snowstorm that allowed the men of the 80th to return to their lines, taking with them the wounded and frostbitten but the 80th Regiment "Roma" was finally unblock and the Russians retreated.
